# Dismiss floating menus and pickers on outside pointers

## Context

A downstream right-click menu report exposed a focus-management assumption that was independently reproduced on Engine `dev` head `17b59aad8f95c55c916fd6bb8bd6a0f43bd2d687`.

A temporary complete Neo Body app opened a floating `Neo.menu.List` from `onContextMenu` using real browser pointer input. Nested first- and second-level submenus stayed open on this machine, so the reported submenu loss is timing/load-sensitive rather than universal. Outside dismissal was deterministically broken: clicking a non-focusable application surface left the menu item as `document.activeElement` and all menus mounted, both with and without `parentComponent`. Making that surface focusable caused the existing focus-leave path to dismiss correctly.

The same control against `Neo.form.field.ComboBox` reproduced the shared limitation: clicking non-focusable application chrome left the input focused and the Picker expanded. The Picker works when focus moves; it is not pointer-complete.

## The Problem

Focus and pointer containment are related but not interchangeable:

- `Neo.menu.List` schedules root hide/unmount through a hard-coded 20ms timeout after `menuFocus=false`. The timeout was intended as approximately one animation frame, but App→VDom→Main→App focus propagation can exceed it.
- Submenus bubble `menuFocus` back to their parent after mount/focus. A frame-sized timer can therefore unmount the root before structurally valid submenu focus arrives.
- `menu.List` and `form.field.Picker` dismiss only when focus leaves their interaction islands. Clicking non-focusable workspace chrome may not move focus at all, so no focus event can close the floating surface.
- Application-root mousedown workarounds solve one app while leaving the framework contract undiscoverable and easy to implement inconsistently.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/manager/Focus.mjs` already owns the focusout/focusin combination window and component-path transitions. Menu must not add a shorter competing correctness timer.
- `src/form/field/Picker.mjs` demonstrates the correct two-sided focus-island shape: field focus-leave checks the picker path, and picker focus-leave checks the field path.
- `src/menu/List.mjs` has a larger interaction island: the current menu, every mounted descendant submenu, and the exact string `align.target` trigger anchor. `parentComponent` remains logical ancestry; it is not automatically a pointer-inside trigger.
- `Neo.mixin.DomEvents#addDomListeners()` / `removeDomListeners()` allow a floating owner to attach a scoped `mousedown` listener to its own app main view. The App worker already receives component-path data; no new Main-thread global registry is required.
- Button menus must keep their trigger inside the interaction island so a trigger click continues to toggle closed rather than close on mousedown and reopen on click. Every shipped Button-menu factory binds `align.target` to the Button id, making that identity exact.

## The Fix

1. Add pointer-outside dismissal to floating root Menu lists and Pickers while visible/mounted by attaching one scoped App-main-view `mousedown` listener and removing the exact listener on hide/unmount/destroy.
2. Menu path classification treats the root, every mounted descendant submenu, and an exact string `align.target` trigger anchor as inside. Picker classification treats the field and picker subtree as inside. A serialized coordinate target deliberately has no trigger element.
3. An outside pointer dismisses even when `document.activeElement` does not change. Inside pointer interactions never dismiss.
4. Remove the 20ms frame heuristic as a Menu correctness gate. Model Menu focus partners structurally, mirroring Picker's two-sided checks; animation timing may not decide ownership.
5. Add focused Menu and Picker unit coverage for focusable and non-focusable outside paths, nested submenu transitions, trigger toggling, Escape, and exact listener teardown.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Floating root `Neo.menu.List` dismissal | Existing Menu focus/parent/submenu model | Dismiss on pointer outside the complete menu interaction island, independent of focus movement | Inline lists do not register outside dismissal; exact string `align.target` trigger anchors and mounted menu paths stay inside | Menu JSDoc | Menu focus/pointer unit matrix |
| `Neo.form.field.Picker` dismissal | Existing two-sided field/picker focus contract | Hide on pointer outside field+picker even when focus remains on the input | Inside field/picker pointer preserves the picker | Picker JSDoc | Picker focusable/non-focusable controls |
| Menu submenu focus ownership | `parentMenu`, `activeSubMenu`, `subMenuMap`, `manager.Focus` paths | Parent and descendant menus remain one logical focus island without a frame-sized correctness timer | True document blur, tab-out, outside pointer, Escape, and leaf policy still dismiss | Explain structural partners | Delayed/ordered focus controls without sleeps as assertions |
| App-root DOM listener lifecycle | Existing `addDomListeners()` / `removeDomListeners()` | One scoped listener exists only while needed and is removed by identity | Reopen is idempotent; destroy leaves no listener | Anchor teardown | Listener-count and destroy controls |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — this completes existing Menu and Picker interaction contracts using their current App-worker event/focus owners.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A real-equivalent outside `mousedown` closes Menu and Picker when the target path is non-focusable and focus does not move.
- [ ] Clicking inside the root menu, any nested submenu, the Button trigger, the Picker field, or the Picker body never triggers outside dismissal.
- [ ] First- and second-level submenu focus survives without a 20ms correctness timer.
- [ ] Focus tab-out, document blur, Escape, Menu leaf policy, and Button trigger toggling retain their current semantics.
- [ ] App-root listeners are added once, removed by exact config identity, and absent after hide/unmount/destroy.
- [ ] Picker coverage is limited to the shared dismissal/focus contract; current selection/typeahead behavior stays green.

## Out of Scope

- Alignment, pointer-coordinate placement, viewport constraint/flip, or the permanent context-menu example.
- Renaming `pickerIsMounted`, removing `clientRects`, or general Picker cleanup.
- A generic overlay manager, new Main-thread event registry, focus-manager timing changes, or document listeners in applications.
- Touch long-press context-menu semantics.

## Avoided Traps

- **Longer timeout:** moves the race without defining ownership.
- **Force every app surface focusable:** changes keyboard navigation to compensate for pointer dismissal.
- **Treat the whole parent widget as context-menu focus:** prevents ordinary clicks within that widget from dismissing.
- **Main-thread singleton:** unnecessary; the App worker already owns component paths and lifecycle.

* fix(menu): a leaf click closes the whole menu tree again (#17850)

Clicking a leaf inside a submenu ran its handler, unmounted that submenu, and left every menu
above it open — an orphaned menu hanging over the app after the chosen action had already run.

`afterSetMenuFocus` is the only path that closes ancestors: a non-root menu bubbles to
`parentMenu`, recursing until the floating root unmounts itself and cascades back down through
`hideSubMenu()`. `onKeyDownEnter` reached `unmount()` directly instead, and #17825 had added

    this._menuFocus = false;

to `unmount()`. The underscore is the defect. It bypasses the config setter, so `afterSetMenuFocus`
never runs and no ancestor is ever told. It also disarmed the fallback: `onFocusLeave` later writes
`menuFocus = false` over an already-false value, the setter sees no change, and that hook stays
silent too.

The silent write is right where it is — reaching `unmount()` FROM `afterSetMenuFocus` must not
re-enter that hook. So the leaf-click path now propagates through the setter before unmounting, and
guards the follow-up on `mounted` because the root's cascade may already have taken this level down.

Verified three ways, at depth 3, in `examples/menu/context/`:

    right-click -> Inspect -> Details -> click "Copy name"
      mounted menus after the click ... 0     (was: the root and Inspect stayed open)
      "Last action: Copy name" .......  set   (the handler still runs)

    outside pointer-down ............... 0     #17825 dismissal intact
    Escape ............................. 0     unchanged

Unit coverage lands in the existing dismissal describe and is mutation-checked: with the source fix
stashed it FAILS on `rootDismissals`, with the fix it passes. Depth 2 on purpose — at depth 1 the
root IS the parent, so closing only the clicked menu passes by accident.

The spec file gains the `manager/Instance` import its sibling `ListTreeStore.spec.mjs` already
carries; without it, touching a store reaches `getController()` -> `Neo.get`, which the unit
harness does not stand up.

22 menu specs and 4 tree specs pass.

* test(menu): witness the cascade, not the intent to cascade (#17850)

Euclid's P1 on PR #17852 is correct: the first version stubbed `root.unmount()` and `level2.unmount()`
with counters, never wired `activeSubMenu`, and never asserted any `mounted` state. It therefore
proved the root was TOLD to unmount, and would have passed with `level1` still mounted — the exact
visible regression #17850 names.

`hideSubMenu()` follows `activeSubMenu`, not `subMenuMap`, so that is what makes an ancestor's
`unmount()` reach its descendants. `Neo.applyDeltas` is already stubbed by the unit setup, so nothing
needs replacing with a counter: the levels really unmount and `mounted` is the witness.

- `createTree()` wires root -> level1 -> level2 through `activeSubMenu` and primes the focus chain.
- The regression test now asserts `mounted === false` on all three levels.
- AC-6 gains a real control: `hideOnLeafItemClick: false` must leave all three mounted and
  `menuFocus` untouched, so the policy gate is shown to govern the new setter write and not only the
  unmount that follows it.

Mutation control redone properly, and the first attempt was hollow: `git stash push -- src/menu/List.mjs`
stashed nothing because the fix was already committed, so the "unfixed" run silently exercised the
fixed code and reported green. Reverting the file to `origin/dev` instead gives the real result, and
it fails on the right line:

    236 |  expect(level2.mounted).toBe(false);    passes — level2 does close when broken
  > 237 |  expect(level1.mounted).toBe(false);    Expected: false  Received: true

23 menu specs pass with the fix.

* test(menu): witness the cascade in a browser, where the defect lives (#17850)

The unit witness added in 2a8bb80 asserts `mounted` on all three levels, and it
is real -- it fails on the unfixed source. It is also not enough, and this PR
should not claim it is: it runs with `Neo.applyDeltas` stubbed, so it measures
worker-side state and never the DOM a user looks at.

Two measurements, both against `origin/dev` with the fix reverted:

1. A browser witness written the obvious way ALSO passes on the regression.
   `expect(page.locator('.neo-menu-list')).toHaveCount(0)` is web-first and
   re-polls until the timeout, and on the unfixed source the tree does reach
   zero -- a later focus round-trip sweeps the ancestors up. The settled state
   is identical either way. The defect is the transient.

2. `e2e/rendering/ContextMenuNL.spec.mjs` already carried exactly that
   assertion, and it passes on the unfixed source. So the one spec that claimed
   to prove leaf-click dismissal was blind to this defect class before it was
   blind for any reason involving CI.

Recording the level-count transitions across the click makes the lingering
ancestors an observation instead of a state polled past:

    unfixed: [3, 2, 0]     the clicked submenu closes alone
    fixed  : [3, 0]        the whole tree goes together

The new spec lives in the components tier because that is a tier CI runs, on a
path (`src/`) that triggers it -- real main thread, real App worker, real
pointer input, no Brain runtime. `ContextMenuNL` gets the same witness so its
cascade claim is true, though the e2e suite runs in no CI workflow at all;
that gap is its own ticket, not this one.

Verified: components 82/82, unit/menu 23/23, both new arms red on the reverted
fix at the transition assertion and green on it."
